heading: Island shape lab
hint: Compares seeds and generation parameters side by side using the same worldGenerator.ts port the game runs client-side — nothing here calls the backend.
docsIntro: Each island is a bent spine of vertices with a width each (a crescent, a C, a wandering ridge) plus a few satellite islets, all warped by a two-octave coastline warp (fjords, bays, headlands) and roughened by three octaves of shoreline noise. Every island cell rolls a size class: mostly medium (B), some small (A) and a few large (C, which also clear the cells around them).
docsFields: Half-width min/max: how wide a medium island's body is before its class scale. Spine segments: how many vertices the spine is walked through. Elongation min/max: total spine length as a multiple of the half-width. Bend min/max: how tightly the spine curls (0 straight, 0.35 a tight C). Coast warp / warp wavelength: amplitude and wavelength of the large-scale warp. Coast roughness / roughness wavelength: amplitude and wavelength of the shoreline noise. Small / large share: the share of cells holding an A or a C island.
docsBudget: An island is never cut at its cell border or at the world edge: it is shrunk to fit its max reach (each hex scans as many rings of cells as that needs; 0 is the legacy rule, the 3x3 block of cells around its own), and an island that could reach past the world radius is not generated at all. Min sea gap: an island whose nominal coast comes closer than this to a larger (or same-class, higher-rolled) neighbour is not generated, so islands never fuse into blobs (0 switches it off).
